evidence_for_A: Captures full date YYYY-MM-DD in a single capture group: (\d{4}-(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01]))
Uses (?![\w-]) to prevent alphanumeric/hyphen following the date, satisfying the false-match requirement
Uses negative lookahead to ensure the matched date is the last date in the line
Year is 4 digits (\d{4}) which is more general and matches typical date format requirements
evidence_for_B: Capture group only captures the year ((?:19|20)\d{2}), not the full date, so re.findall returns only the year portion, not the full YYYY-MM-DD
Restricts year to 19xx/20xx which may reject valid test dates outside that range
Lacks a lookahead/lookbehind guarding against trailing alphanumeric right after the day component
result.reason: Attempt A passes the verifier and correctly captures the full date in a single group while enforcing word-boundary/false-match constraints and last-date-in-line logic. Attempt B fails the verifier, primarily because its capture group only captures the year portion, so re.findall would return only years rather than full dates, and it narrows the year range unnecessarily.
